title: Six Decades of Asymmetric Hydroclimate Change at Lamto, Côte d’Ivoire
content: We analysed daily precipitation and minimum and maximum temperatures at Lamto, Côte d’Ivoire, from 1964 to 2023 to assess changes in means, extremes, and their seasonal relationships with tropical Pacific and Atlantic sea-surface-temperature anomalies. Sen slopes, dependence-aware tests, and explicit false-discovery-rate families distinguished trend magnitude from inferential support. Annual precipitation showed no detectable monotonic trend (+3.49 mm decade−1; individual 95% confidence interval (CI) −29.61 to +33.96), and no annual precipitation-extreme index showed a statistically significant trend after adjustment for multiple testing. Annual Tmin, Tmean and Tmax increased by 0.18, 0.25 and 0.35 °C decade−1, respectively, with increases in sea-sonal mean temperature, hottest-day temperature, and warm-day and warm-night frequencies across all four climatic phases. September–November maximum daily rainfall increased by 4.00 mm decade−1, whereas evidence for trends in seasonal rainfall totals, five-day rainfall maxima, and dry-spell duration depended on the statistical method used. After removing their long-term trends, annual rainfall and temperature were weakly related. Additionally, seasonal temperatures and some rainfall characteristics were associated with Pacific and Atlantic Ocean-temperature varia-tions, with most findings holding across different uncertainty-estimation methods. Overall, Lamto experienced annual and seasonal warming alongside more selective changes in rainfall. Although some seasonal variations were associated with tropical ocean temperatures, these relationships do not establish the cause of long-term warming. Moreover, an unresolved discontinuity in Tmin limits interpretation of nighttime trends, highlighting the need for independent observations to verify daytime–nighttime warming contrasts and to investigate the ocean links.
